result.topic_en: Gauss defines the infinite product $(1+xy)(1+x^3y)(1+x^5y)\cdots(1+x/y)(1+x^3/y)\cdots$ as $(x,y)$ and derives product/addition theorems (numbered 69–72) for it, as part of the theory of the 'Fünfeck' (pentagon) / theta-type series.
result.transcription:
Litt. f.

Zu der Theorie der Fünfecke[?] gehören folgende Theoreme
Ich bezeichne $(1+xy)(1+x^3y)(1+x^5y)\cdots(1+\frac{x}{y})(1+\frac{x^3}{y})(1+\frac{x^5}{y})\cdots$ durch $(x,y)$: so ist

[69] $(x,\alpha y)\cdot(x,\frac{y}{\alpha}) = P(1+xx(yy+\frac{1}{yy})+x^8(y^4+\frac{1}{y^4})\cdots)$
$+Q(y+\frac{1}{y}+x^4(y^3+\frac{1}{y^3})+x^{12}(y^5+\frac{1}{y^5})\cdots)$
wo $P$, $Q$ von $y$ unabhängig

Man kann auch leicht die Reihe womit P mult. ist, $=0$ machen ist $y=\frac{1}{x}\sqrt{-1}$[?]

Also
$(x,\alpha i)(x,\frac{\alpha}{i}) = (xx,\alpha\alpha) = P(1-2xx+2x^8\cdots) = \frac{[xx]^2}{[x^4]}P$ oder
$P=\frac{(xx,\alpha\alpha)[x^4]}{[xx]^2}$
Ferner für $y=-\alpha x$
$(x,-\alpha x)\cdot(x,-x)=0=P(1+\frac{1}{\alpha\alpha}+\alpha\alpha x^4+\frac{x^4}{\alpha^4}+)-Q(\alpha x+\frac{1}{\alpha x}+\frac{x}{\alpha^3}+\alpha^3x^7+\frac{x^7}{\alpha^5})$
d.i. $P(\alpha+\frac{1}{\alpha}+x^4(\alpha^3+\frac{1}{\alpha^3})+x^{12}(\alpha^5+\frac{1}{\alpha^5})\cdots) = \frac{Q}{x}(1+xx(\alpha\alpha+\frac{1}{\alpha\alpha})+x^8(\alpha^4+\frac{1}{\alpha^4})\cdots)$
Nun ist $P=\frac{1}{[xx]^2}(1+xx(\alpha\alpha+\frac{1}{\alpha\alpha})+$ etc.
Also $Q=\frac{x}{[xx]^2}((\alpha+\frac{1}{\alpha})+x^4(\alpha^3+\frac{1}{\alpha^3})\cdots)$ u. unser Theorem

(70) $(x,\alpha y)(x,\frac{y}{\alpha}) = \frac{1}{[xx]^2}\{(1+xx(\alpha\alpha+\frac{1}{\alpha\alpha})+x^8(\alpha^4+\frac{1}{\alpha^4})\cdots)(1+xx(yy+\frac{1}{yy})+x^8(y^4+\frac{1}{y^4})\cdots)$
$+x(\alpha+\frac{1}{\alpha}+x^4(\alpha^3+\frac{1}{\alpha^3})+x^{12}(\alpha^5+\frac{1}{\alpha^5}))(y+\frac{1}{y}+x^4(y^3+\frac{1}{y^3})+x^{12}(y^5+\frac{1}{y^5}))\}$
oder
$(x,\alpha y)\cdot(x,\frac{y}{\alpha}) = \frac{[x^4]^2}{[xx]^2}\{(xx,\alpha\alpha)\cdot(xx,yy)+x\alpha y(xx,\alpha\alpha xx)(xx,xxyy)\}$

$(x,\alpha x) = \frac{1}{\alpha}(x,\frac{x}{\alpha})$
$(x,\alpha xx) = \frac{1}{\alpha x}(x,\alpha)$
$-\frac{y}{x}(-x,-y)$[?]

(71) $(x,y)+(x,\frac{x}{y})\sqrt[4]{\frac{x}{yy}} = (x^{\frac14},y^{\frac12})\frac{[x^{\frac12}]}{[xx]}$
Den Satz 70 kann man auch so ausdrücken

(72) $(x,\alpha)\cdot(x,\beta) = \frac{[x^4]^2}{[xx]^2}\{(xx,\alpha\beta)\cdot(xx,\frac{\alpha}{\beta})+x\alpha(xx,\alpha\beta xx)\cdot(xx,\frac{\alpha xx}{\beta})\}$
Hieraus folgt
$(x,+\frac{x}{\alpha})\cdot(x,+\frac{x}{\beta}) = \frac{[x^4]^2}{[xx]^2}\{(xx,\frac{xx}{\alpha\beta})\cdot(xx,\frac{\alpha}{\beta})+\alpha(xx,\alpha\beta)\cdot(xx,\frac{\alpha xx}{\beta})\}$

methods.what: Notation for a Jacobi-triple-product-type infinite product (theta function)
Product of two theta products expanded as even and odd series in y with coefficients P, Q independent of y
Determination of P by specializing y=i (duplication relation)
Determination of Q by specializing y=-αx (zero of the product)
Theorem 71: relation between products with x and x^{1/4}
Theorem 72: reformulated product theorem in α, β

items.quote: Man kann auch leicht die Reihe womit P mult. ist, $=0$ machen ist $y=\frac{1}{x}\sqrt{-1}$[?]
items.english: One can also easily make the series by which P is multiplied equal to 0, namely with y = (1/x)√−1 [uncertain].
